newsitem.title: USA: Brown Group Q4 hurt by margin squeeze.
newsitem.headline: Brown Group Q4 hurt by margin squeeze.

text.p: Brown Group Inc, posting lower February 1 fourth-quarter net earnings, cited a slower-than-anticipated holiday selling season that resulted in reduced margins in its retail operations.

For the full year, the shoe manufacturer reported significantly higher earnings, which it attributed to the benefits of improved expense leverage, better performance at its Famous Footwear divison and a return to sales gains and solid profitability at Brown Shoe Co's wholesale operations.

Brown Group's fourth-quarter earnings were $0.08 per share compared with $0.36, which included $0.15 per share from discontinued operations. For the full year, earnings jumped to $1.15 per share compared to $0.19 on sales that rose 4.8 percent to $1.53 billion.

"Results for the year reflect the value of the structural changes Brown Group completed in 1995," said chairman B.A. Bridgewater Jr. "Improving operations, higher margins from the shift to all-import sourcing and the repositioning of the company's debt structure in the latter part of the year, position Brown Group for continued progress."

The company said same-store sales at its Famous Footwear were up 1.3 percent for the year. Bridgewater said during 1996, a net of 20 new Famous Footwear stores were added while 40 Naturalizer Outlet stores were transferred to the Naturalizer Retail division at the beginning of the year.
There were 794 stores in operation at fiscal year-end, with a net of 25 new stores planned for 1997.
Naturalizer Retail division sales declined 3.3 percent in the year, and same-store sales declined 1.2 percent. Bridgewater said an operating loss was again recorded.

Brown Shoe Co, which includes both the Brown Branded Marketing and Pagoda divisions, achieved a turnaround, he said. The combined wholesale operations reported operating earnings of $26.8 million compared to a slight loss from operations the prior year.

A new advertising campaign starting this spring for the Naturalizer brand, combined with a further shift to casual and tailored merchandise, will be important to Naturalizer's success in 1997, Bridgewater noted in a statement.

"At the Pagoda division, higher sales of branded and licensed product resulted in operating earnings that were almost double those of last year, despite lower than anticipated results in Pagoda International," Bridgewater said.
